sentences.text: The skull of Altirhinus measured 760 millimeters in length and featured a distinctive high nasal arch, which gives the genus its name.
Altirhinus had a wide mouth containing 26 teeth in the upper jaw, 24 in the lower jaw, a third set of replacement teeth, and ended in a horny beak.
The original description estimated Altirhinus reached a length of 8 meters from snout to tail tip.
A 2010 estimate by Gregory S. Paul placed Altirhinus at 6.5 meters long and weighing 1.1 tonnes.
Altirhinus was a herbivore that walked quadrupedally and ran bipedally, feeding on low vegetation.
Altirhinus possessed a sharp spike on its first digit that may have been used for defense or breaking seed and fruit shells.
Altirhinus had a large gap between its beak and chewing teeth, allowing it to crop vegetation with its beak while simultaneously chewing.
All known Altirhinus specimens were found in 1981 by Soviet and Mongolian scientists in the Khuren Dukh Formation of Dornogovi Province, Mongolia.
Fossils now identified as Altirhinus were originally classified as the species Iguanodon orientalis, which was described in 1952.
The genus Altirhinus was named by British paleontologist David B. Norman in 1998.
The holotype of Altirhinus consists of a well-preserved left skull and some postcranial material including hand, foot, shoulder, and pelvic pieces.
Altirhinus was a herbivore that walked or ran on two legs but likely used four legs when feeding on the ground.
Altirhinus's front limbs were about half the length of its hind limbs, suggesting it was primarily bipedal.

However, Altirhinus's wrist bones were thick and cubic, and its three central hand digits were broad, hyperextensible, and ended in hoof-like bones, indicating the front limbs could also support weight.
Like many ornithopods, Altirhinus may have spent significant time in a quadrupedal position, perhaps while feeding.
Besides defense, Altirhinus's thumb claw may have been used to break seed or fruit shells.
The fifth digit was somewhat opposable to the rest of the hand and may have been useful for grasping food.
A large diastema between the horny beak and the tooth battery allowed the two sections to work independently, enabling Altirhinus to crop with its beak while simultaneously chewing with its teeth.
Altirhinus was one of the most advanced iguanodontians with wide mouths flaring outward at the tip.
This wide snout is possibly an example of convergent evolution with hadrosaurids, famous for their wide duck-bill snouts.
The nasal arch may have been used for vocalization, visual display, or sexual display, though evidence is limited to only two skulls.
Altirhinus is classified as an advanced iguanodontian positioned just below the family Hadrosauridae, though its exact placement in the family tree is debated.
In its original description, Altirhinus was placed in the family Iguanodontidae alongside Iguanodon and Ouranosaurus.
Altirhinus is definitely an iguanodontian, just basal to Hadrosauridae, though there is little agreement on the arrangement of genera and species in this area of the ornithopod family tree.
In its original description, Altirhinus was included with Iguanodon and Ouranosaurus in the family Iguanodontidae.
All recent analyses find Altirhinus more derived than Iguanodon and Ouranosaurus, but less derived than Protohadros, Probactrosaurus, and hadrosaurids.
Altirhinus lived during the Early Cretaceous period, specifically from the Barremian to the Albian stages.
Altirhinus was a hadrosauroid ornithopod dinosaur that lived in Mongolia during the Early Cretaceous period.
Altirhinus kurzanovi was the only known species in the extinct genus, living in Asia during the Middle Cretaceous, approximately 110 million years ago in the Albian stage.
Altirhinus lived during the Aptian and Albian stages of the Early Cretaceous, approximately 125 to 100 million years ago.
Researchers have proposed various functions for Altirhinus's nasal arch, including cooling blood, conserving water, or enhancing the sense of smell.
Alternatively, the nasal arch may have facilitated communication through vocalization or visual display.
Given that only two skulls are known, it is possible the arched snout was used for sexual display, similar to modern elephant seals.
